description: Both fertilizer and seeds need to be added to a lawn. One unit of fertilizer takes 0.5 minutes to be effective while one unit of seeds takes 1.5 minutes to be effective. There can be at most 300 units of fertilizer and seeds combined added to the lawn. In addition at least 50 units of fertilizer need to be added. Since the lawn is really patchy, there can be at most twice the amount of fertilizer as seeds. How many units of each should be added to minimize the total time it takes for the lawn to be ready?

TimePerFertilizer.definition: Time one unit of fertilizer takes to be effective

TimePerSeeds.definition: Time one unit of seeds takes to be effective

MaxTotalUnits.definition: Maximum total units of fertilizer and seeds combined

MinFertilizer.definition: Minimum units of fertilizer to be added

MaxFertilizerRatio.definition: Maximum ratio of fertilizer to seeds

objective.description: "Minimize the total time required for the fertilizer and seeds to be effective, i.e., minimize the total time for the lawn to be ready."

constraints.description: The total units of fertilizer and seeds combined should not exceed MaxTotalUnits
The units of fertilizer added should be at least MinFertilizer
The units of fertilizer should not exceed MaxFertilizerRatio times the units of seeds

FertilizerUnits.definition: Total units of fertilizer added to the lawn

SeedsUnits.definition: Total units of seeds added to the lawn
